Then, by adjusting the loop bandwidth, it can reduce the convergence time of the acquisition-state and carrier jitter of the steady state. The new scheme, implemented by FPGAs, has been successfully applied to a 256-QAM baseband digital receiver and inter-operated with commercial CMTSs. Only around 11200 gates are needed for the new carrier synchronizer; however, the SNR can be improved by up to 3 dB.

articleTitle: Color reproduction error correction for color temperature conversion in PDP-TV
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: An efficient method of correcting color reproduction error is proposed for displaying the NTSC-based video signal in PDP-TV and is also shown to be successfully coupled with flexible color temperature conversion based on the signal processing technique.

articleTitle: MPEG-2 to MPEG-4 transcoder using object-based motion vector clustering
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We present an MPEG-2 to MPEG-4 transcoder using an object-based motion vector clustering (OMVC) method which can skip frames dynamically and reduce the spatial resolution of frames arbitrarily. Experimental results show that the proposed transcoder using the OMVC method outperforms the existing method with better visual quality.

articleTitle: Considerations about an HDD-based removable medium and its AT-attachment interface architecture for copyright protection
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper describes the concept of a novel removable medium based on a hard disk drive (called iVDR/spl trade/-: for information versatile disk for removable usage) and an interface architecture for copyright protection based on public key infrastructure (PKI) and superdistribution. This interface architecture is applicable to various media including iVDR whose interfaces are AT-attachment (ATA) based.

articleTitle: MPEG-4 FAP generation as an optimization problem
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper presents a method for automatic generation of FAPs (facial animation parameters) based on a video sequence. An FAP generating unit compares an animated face with the original face in the video sequence. The difference is iteratively minimized to produce an optimal set of FAPs. The resulting FAPs are accurate and the animated face is lifelike and truthful to the original video.

articleTitle: Changes in US FCC spectrum policy affecting consumer electronic devices
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The US Federal Communications Commission has recently initiated a process to overhaul spectrum policy in an effort to modernize how spectrum is managed in the US. These changes are likely to alter significantly spectrum usage for wireless product categories and may directly affect design parameters for some receivers. The paper discusses the findings of the FCC's Spectrum Policy Task Force, which proposes a number of changes in spectrum policy and for which the FCC has solicited public comments. The paper goes on to examine the implications for "unlicensed" devices and broadcast receivers.

articleTitle: A fast DCT domain downsampling technique for video transcoder
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a fast DCT domain downsampling technique for video transcoding. Experimental results show that the proposed method is not only computationally efficient, but also gives significant improvements in PSNR.

articleTitle: Self-configuring and auto-executing audio-visual system for consumer use
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We describe a consumer-use, self-configurable, auto-executable audio-visual system using reasoning technology, and confirm its feasibility through evaluation using an embedded microprocessor with minimum operation.

articleTitle: Organic thin film transistors based on anthracene oligomers
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Organic thin-film transistors (OTFTs) were fabricated using organic semiconductor anthracene oligomers, 2,2'-bianthracene (2A), 2,6-trianthracene (3A), and their dihexyl derivatives (DH-2A and DH-3A), as the active layer material. X-ray diffraction and atomic force microscopy revealed that the thin films of anthracene oligomers deposited by thermal evaporation had a high degree of lamellar ordering. The OTFTs showed high field effect mobilities; the highest mobility (0.13 cm/sup 2//Vs) was obtained for DH-2A.

articleTitle: Communication of remote control key codes in the home network
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper describes CEA-931-A, a standard method for communication of remote control unit (RCU) key presses across the home audio/video network. The new standard is also applicable where "infrared blaster" techniques were previously employed, offering many benefits.

articleTitle: A novel distributed speech recognition platform for wireless mobile devices
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: A novel distributed speech recognition (DSR) development platform, configurable DSR (C-DSR), is proposed for various kinds of wireless devices to remotely configure and employ sophisticated recognizers on the server over wireless networks. Many portable speech recognition applications, such as voice-controlled toys, TV remotes, vehicle navigator and mobile inquiry systems were efficiently deployed using C-DSR platform over WLAN/GPRS by simply configuring their configuration files from client side.

articleTitle: Fast scene change detection for personal video recorder
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a fast scene change detection algorithm suitable for personal video recorders with a low powered CPU using reduced images of intra pictures in the MPEG-2 compressed domain.

articleTitle: Disparity-compensated coding using MAC for stereoscopic video
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a novel disparity-compensated coding algorithm using MAC (multiple auxiliary component) of MPEG-4 for stereoscopic video. MAC was added to the MPEG-4 visual version 2 in order to describe the transparency of the video object. The major difference between the existing coding method and the proposed coding method is the addition of the residual texture coding. The proposed coding method assigns disparity map and residual texture to 3 components of MAC: one component for disparity map and the remaining 2 components for the luminance and chrominance data of the residual texture, respectively.

articleTitle: The HM12000 framework: a flexible software architecture for embedded multimedia systems
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The multimedia systems introduced by leading car manufacturers mark a new level of functional integration, networking and graphical user interface. In this paper some requirements of a novel software architecture for these systems are presented. Then we discuss the object-oriented framework, which forms the common software basis for several of these embedded automotive multimedia systems, and how the requirements are implemented.

articleTitle: A constant-quality, single-pass VBR control for DVD recorders
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper describes a low complexity variable bit-rate (VBR) control method that achieves excellent and constant visual quality for single-pass, real time MPEG-2 encoding in DVD recorders. The bit-rate is controlled in a very accurate way.

articleTitle: A low cost smell detection system for multimedia applications
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: A multimedia system is one of the most widely used consumer electronics environments today in which humans can work or communicate through multi-sensory interfaces. Existing multimedia systems include audio systems and video displays that make use of the human auditory and visual systems. The minor sensory information namely, smell, taste and touch are generally not used. In order to use smell in multimedia environments, smell detectors and producers are required. We propose a low cost smell detector that can be used in a multimedia environment. It is shown that a crude smell detection system, which can detect tens of smells can be developed at a low cost, compared to that of typical systems used in industrial applications.

articleTitle: TV4U: full personalized TV
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative concept of a service that integrates a TV type of passive service and a Web type of active service. We have developed a prototype fully-personalized TV system called "TV4U" which has the following two features: (1) individual tailoring of TV programs (My Variety) allows the user to customize and enjoy their own tailored information variety programs, and (2) interaction with TV presenters (Seamless Interaction) allows the user to break into the running program and have a dialogue with the TV presenter directly to get more information. In the TV4U system, the TV set has a built-in computer to create personalized TV programs using real-time computer graphics (CG), voice synthesis and other multimedia functions. On the other hand, all the necessary information for automatically producing the TV programs is acquired from the Internet, PC and home server via the network connected to the TV set. We have built and tested a prototype of this TV4U system.

articleTitle: Toward user oriented scalable video by using foveated FGS bitstreams
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: A human visual system model, foveation, is used to provide user-oriented video scalability, which benefits those applications concerning user's regions of interest. Based on processing FGS-coded (fine granularity scalable coded) videos, we show that the proposed method has tolerable complexity and is standard compliant.

articleTitle: SonarPen: a new ultrasonic pointing device for an interactive TV
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: An interactive TV demands more sophisticated forms of interaction than traditional remotes can provide. A variety of technologies and interaction techniques exist for remote pointing. We introduce an ultrasonic pointing device for an interactive TV that guarantees directness in pointing operations.

articleTitle: A person annotation overlay using a wearable computer for augmented reality
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a person annotation overlay system using a wearable computer for augmented reality environment which allows the user to recognize an unknown person. The system uses a combination of color and edge information to detect the face. Then, the system is applied to recognize multiple persons based on the face dictionary. Experimental results show that the proposed system is applicable to a visitor guider.

articleTitle: Automatic video summarizing tool using MPEG-7 descriptors for STB
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We introduce a video summarizing tool for a set-top box. The tool utilizes MPEG-7 visual descriptors in generating video summary index. The resulting index can offer not only a preview of movie but also non-linear access with thumbnail images. In addition, the index supports searching of similar shots to a desired one within saved video sequences. Moreover, a simple shot-based video editing can be achieved by the generated index.

articleTitle: Area effective and wide applicable architecture of error correction and detection for digital home network platform
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: An area effective and widely applicable architecture for error correction is described, which we apply to a cable modem prototype. We implemented new procedure for a RS decoder, and adopted a new architecture for CRC operation.

articleTitle: Carrier estimation, time synchronization, and adaptive equalization with pilot estimation for 8-VSB ATSC terrestrial receivers .1
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We address the problem of carrier recovery, time synchronization, and pilot estimation for 8-VSB HDTV North American terrestrial receivers.

articleTitle: Indoor use high-bit rate infrared wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We developed a wireless infrared communication system that uses a data rate of 150 Mbps. It does not interfere with the infrared remote controller, wireless head-phone, and other infrared communications. Our system uses a PIN PD and an LED.

articleTitle: An MPEG-4 video codec SOC for mobile multimedia applications
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Mobile multimedia is foreseen as one of the major applications for the upcoming broadband mobile networks like UMTS. Besides pure streaming applications for uni-directional communication, bi-directional applications like video teleconferencing and multimedia messaging will become increasingly popular. The paper aims to provide an overview about the implementation of an ASIC suited for mobile multimedia applications. The ASIC features a complete single chip solution for MPEG-4 video coding and decoding, using picture resolutions of up to QCIF @ 15 fps and data rates up to 128 kbit/s based on several hardware acceleration components and an embedded processor. After an introduction of the incorporated MPEG-4 video standard and the targeted applications of the ASIC, the paper gives a overview of the structure of the encoder and the decoder.

articleTitle: Embedded implementation of acoustic field enhancement for stereo sound sources
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: An embedded implementation of acoustic field enhancement is proposed, which is dedicated to stereo sound sources. With the use of the embedded DSP-base platform, this algorithm successfully constructs the signal processing filter structure to enhance a 3D acoustic field through either of stereo headphones and stereo speakers. The whole of proposed algorithm can be implemented by a 16 bit fixed-point DSP with the computational costs of 51.6 MIPS and 6.6 kB of memory, high-fidelity spatial acoustics can be achieved in various applications, such as portable stereo players, music streaming to mobile devices, etc.

articleTitle: A seamless coordinator switching (SCS) scheme for wireless personal area network (WPAN)
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: In the emerging wireless personal area networks (WPAN), one of the active devices in a piconet is designated as a coordinator, which plays critical roles, e.g., to provide the basic timing for the piconet and manage the QoS requirements/power saving modes. To warrant maintenance of the coordinating function under some unpredictable situations such as sudden power-off or fast movement, a coordinator must be seamlessly switched. This paper proposes a new SCS (seamless coordinator switching) scheme to maintain the piconet by selecting a coordinator in the subsequent superframe without incurring the re-initialization overhead.

articleTitle: Carrier estimation, time synchronization, and adaptive equalization with pilot estimation for 8-VSB ATSC terrestrial receivers .2
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: For pt.1 see ibid., p.116-17 (2003).This second part of the paper motivates the use of adaptive estimation of the DC offset at the receiver and gives an interpretation of the result furnished by a joint optimization over the DC offset estimate and the equalizer parameters of the constant modulus cost function. It is shown that, for an arbitrary DC offset, the CM cost function admits spurious local minima in terms of equalizer settings. Extrema of the cost function in terms or a DC offset are derived and classified, and simple effective adaptive methods for DC offset estimation are discussed. It is shown that these methods lead to equalizer settings equivalent to those furnished by CM equalization with an unbiased source.

articleTitle: An EAA traffic conditioner in differential services home gateway
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The file sizes of on going flows are fairly disparate on the home network environment. We propose an "age-based" packet discard scheme in the traffic conditioner (TC) of a home gateway (HG), which is referred as EAA model, to improve the performance of file transmission. The on going flows will be grouped to three classes of priority according to their "age" as the HG congestion occurs and the simulation results show that the proposed model can work efficiently in most of the congestion conditions.

articleTitle: A computational efficient method for bandwidth extension of a conference phone
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper presents a computational efficient method for extension of the bandwidth of a conference phone. The virtue of the proposed method is that it allows an improvement in quality, i.e. increased bandwidth, at virtually no extra computational cost. Frequency analysis in combination with subjective tests showed that the proposed method extends the bandwidth without introducing any artifacts.

articleTitle: BIFS extension for augmented stereoscopic video
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: In this paper, the extended BIFS (Binary Format for Scene) of MPEG (Moving Picture Experts Group)-4 is proposed for augmented stereoscopic video. BIFS is a scene graph for MPEG-4, and is based on VRML (Virtual Reality Markup Language). ASV (augmented stereoscopic video) is thought as an off-line AR (augmented reality). Thus, there are some mismatch problems when augmented stereoscopic video presents in BIFS. In AR, the registration is a key technology. BIFS does not support that. We introduce a registration mechanism to BIFS. Also, in this paper new nodes are proposed for stereoscopic and camera information stream.

articleTitle: Cost driven six sigma analysis for CE software development
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Increased software demands from consumers lead CE (consumer electronics) companies towards a shift from hardware-oriented to a more software-oriented industry. Many CE companies spend a tremendous amount of money on software development and post release defect fixing. We propose a modification of the traditional six sigma approach to fully analyze and measure software development cost.

articleTitle: High-speed DVD-multi drive system
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: High speed DVD-RAM and DVD-R recording technologies have been established for the DVD-multi drive system. The developed key components are LSIs, especially a laser diode driver, and an optical pickup.

articleTitle: An adaptive global enhancement pipeline for low cost imaging sensors
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The paper describes a suitable pipeline algorithm that is able to enhance the picture quality of low cost imaging sensors, typically present in consumer devices (i.e. mobile phone, Web-cams, PDA, etc.) and accounts for compression artifacts, chromatic and geometric distortions, wrong exposure and poor sharpness.

articleTitle: Real-time frame-layer rate control for low bit rate video over WLAN
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The paper presents a new real-time frame-layer rate control for low bit rate video over WLAN. Compared with the conventional TMN8, the proposed algorithm significantly improves the quality of the compressed video in both objective and subjective tests.

articleTitle: An MPEG-4/7 based architecture for analyzing and retrieving news video programs
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: An MPEG-4/7 based architecture is proposed for analyzing and retrieving news video programs. The proposed architecture covers all stages of a content flow, such as creation, composition and presentation.

articleTitle: Reliable detection of video watermarks using inferential statistics
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Errors in watermark detection can cause serious problems, such as erroneous copy control and misindication of illegal copying. This paper proposes a new watermark method which prevents detection errors by using the expectation-maximization algorithm from inferential statistics. Experimental evaluations have confirmed its reliability.

articleTitle: Improved error detection and concealment techniques for MPEG-4
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper describes new methods for errors treatment at the MPEG-4 decoder side, in the case of channel disturbances, for obtaining high quality performances.

articleTitle: A low cost wireless multimedia player based on 802.11b
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low cost wireless multimedia player based on the IEEE 802.11b wireless protocol. By using this wireless protocol, the multimedia streams are transmitted from a server over the Ethernet to an AP (access point). Moreover, every player can receive signals in the wireless environment. According to the open source feature, the budgets of the software development tools in drivers, OS kernel, GUI interface, audio/video output library, and application programs are free. Furthermore, we sift the hardware components from general multi-function devices. By taking these advantages, the cost could be greatly reduced.

articleTitle: The development of MPEG-7 interface over MPEG-4
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Lately, there has been a vast increase in interactive broadcasting contents research using the MPEG-4 standard and in multimedia content description research using the MPEG-7 standard. Also, there are few researches into a compromise between the MPEG-4 standard and the MPEG-7 standard for newer applications, such as an interactive broadcasting contents server, which is able to query and search. The paper presents the first results of research on the MPEG-7 interface over MPEG-4 systems, which makes it easy to search MPEG-4 content. We have developed an MPEG-7 interface embedded in MPEG-4 systems and an MPEG-4 player that provides a query function and a search function.

articleTitle: Timing-offset compensation techniques in ATSC DTV receivers
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The paper presents symbol timing-offset compensation techniques to improve the reception performance of ATSC DTV receivers. Short and long echoes can induce timing-offset in the symbol timing recovery circuit. The timing-offset shifts sampling instants to the wrong points, causing the performance of the equalizer to become poor. When many echoes exist, the optimal sampling instant is the point at which the main-path has a peak value. By using channel estimation techniques, we find the optimal sampling instant, thereby compensating the timing offset and improving DTV reception performance.

articleTitle: An investigation of an MPEG-4 embedded spatial digital watermark developed for tamper detection and characterization
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The widespread adoption of digital video techniques has generated a requirement for authenticity verification in applications such as criminal evidence, insurance claims and commercial databases. The paper investigates the performance, effectivity and efficiency of a spatial digital watermark designed for video authentication. The embedded watermark is estimated from the possible tampered frame with the use of a temporal filter and the motion information. The imperceptible digital stamp is robustly embedded prior to encoding (compression) and allows tamper characterisation of time-base attacks. The functionality of this system is evaluated within an MPEG-4 implementation.

articleTitle: 50 GB-capacity dual-layer Blu-ray Disc with GeSbTe based phase-change films
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: GeSbTe-based thin films showed superior properties for a recording layer of Blu-ray Disc, especially for a front-side recording layer of L1. The film can be thinned to 6 nm with maintaining a rapid phase-transition rate and a large transmittance of >50% was realized in the L1. It is remarkable that transmittances are balanced between in the amorphous and crystalline areas of L1, and it works to remove the optical interference when recording-playing on the rear-side recording layer of L0 through the L1.

articleTitle: A measurement-based resource allocation for QoS provisioning over IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a measurement-based VBR control that adjusts the coding rates according to the channel characteristics of the wireless-to-wired network. This method can reduce substantially the abrupt quality degradation caused by the change of network condition and scene characteristics.

articleTitle: Novel plasma display driver with low voltage/current device stresses
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: A new energy-recovery-sustain circuit suitable for a plasma display panel (PDP) application is proposed. The proposed circuit features the low device voltage/current stresses, and the inherent circulating current elimination characteristics, essential to design a power efficient and low cost plasma display driver circuit. The proposed circuit is demonstrated experimentally for driving a 42-inch plasma display panel. It is best suited in a low cost and power efficient plasma display.

articleTitle: A simplified multi-antenna reception method of OFDM signal
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: An OFDM diversity receiver of which the dimension of the DFT is reduced is proposed. Symbol reconstruction schemes are discussed and analyzed by computer simulations. As the results, the proposed receiver can achieve better performance than the single antenna receiver keeping the dimension of the DFT the same as that of the single antenna one.

articleTitle: Group digital assistant: shared or combined PDA screen
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper proposes a new concept of a shared and combined screen for new small devices called GDA (group digital assistant). In the GDA, the screens of two PDAs can be shared at a sharing view mode, and can be treated just like one screen at a combination mode. The GDA can change the number of combined screens and direction of those screens flexibly, since the proposal method realizes using radio communications. We have developed application software and experimented in cooperative work for evaluation. We found that functions of the GDA were effective in actual cooperative work. The concept of the GDA can make flexible usage of a cellular phone and a PDA in the next generation.

articleTitle: A unified metric for digital video processing and its applications in home video systems
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: MPEG-2 encoded video is widely used in digital home scenarios. To achieve better performance for MPEG sources, we propose a unified metric for digital video processing, UMDVP. The UMDVP is based on coding information and it also takes the local scene content into account. We have integrated the UMDVP with postprocessing functions such as resolution enhancement and artifact reduction. Experimental results demonstrate the benefit of the proposed metric. Various digital video products can use the new approach to achieve better performance for compressed video.

articleTitle: Generic method for 2D image resizing with simple, non-separable filters
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Low-resolution pictures look bad on high-resolution screens, especially when only simple up-conversion methods like pixel and line repetition or bilinear interpolation are used. Even when applying separable polyphase up-conversion filters, the problem of jagged lines (staircases) remains. The approach investigated for high-quality resizing by rational factors is based on pixel and line repetition with suitable post-filtering. The novel resizing method uses very simple, non-separable filters, and is suitable for all kinds of image and video material such as analog sources (PAL, NTSC) digital sources (JPEG, MPEG), low-resolution up to high-resolution images or photos, and noisy pictures. Jagged lines can be smoothed perfectly.

articleTitle: New processing system for on-line video image retrieval utilizing DSP
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Finding the designated video shots from a video stream within a short time is a big issue in multimedia consumer electronic applications. For a large reduction in the time needed to access the desired video shots, a new system for retrieving the specific shots has been built utilizing on-line motion detection with DSP. Specific video shots can be retrieved at a reduced processing time by using DSP because a series of Y signal image frames and motion vectors are generated on-line by newly utilizing the DSP applications. The image frame codes resulting from the retrieval easily pick up only the designated video shots from the video stream.

articleTitle: Implementation of high performance false contour reduction system using pattern analysis and error-predict method for PDP-HDTV
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper proposes a high performance false contour reduction system with pattern analysis algorithm for PDP-HDTV. It also presents the optimized design and implementation of the method. The proposed method is verified using the Xilinx. Virtex-II FPGA XC2V2000-BG575. Furthermore, we suggest an advanced error-prediction algorithm for high performance. This method is demonstrated experimentally for a 50" PDP-HDTV.

articleTitle: An effective de-interlacing technique using two types of motion information
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a new de-interlacing algorithm using two types of motion information, i.e., the block-based and the pixel-based motion information. In the proposed scheme, block-wise motion is first calculated using the frame differences. Then, it is refined by the pixel-based motion information. The results of hardware implementation show that the proposed scheme using block-wise motion is more robust to noise than the conventional schemes using pixel-wise motion. Also, the proposed spatial interpolation provides a good visual performance in the case of moving diagonal edges.

articleTitle: Small form factor optical Portable Blue drive power consumption considerations
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Optical discs are popular for exchanging and distributing content. A small Portable Blue (SFFO) disc with a diameter of 30 mm stores at least 1 GByte in a single layer using Blu-ray Disc technology. This paper describes strategies to achieve low power consumption in a Portable Blue system. Estimates show a value around 1/20 of the peak (/spl sim/1 W) power while streaming 1 Mb/s data.

articleTitle: A scalable HDD video recording solution using a real-time file system
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We present a scalable solution that enables a single mainstream hard disk drive (HDD) to simultaneously record and play back multiple real-time (RT) video streams, in addition to supporting non-RT PC-like applications. The solution is scalable to different types of disks, different numbers of streams with different bit rates, and various non-RT applications.

articleTitle: Refractive-reflective optical system for realizing ultra-thin rear projector
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: The paper presents a new optical system used in an ultra-thin rear projector with 1500 mm diagonal size and 260 mm depth. A refractive-reflective optical system was developed to achieve a large projection angle of 136 degrees and a small optical distortion of 0.1%. The optics consist of a convex aspherical mirror and a refractive lens. In addition, a new Fresnel screen composed of hybrid blades of refractive-TIR (total internal reflection) elements has been developed to attain good uniformity of brightness and color within the image area.

articleTitle: Metadata engine for TV-Anytime compliant set-top box
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: This paper presents a design of metadata engine based on a relational database architecture for a TV-Anytime compliant set-top box. As TV-Anytime metadata is described in XML, it is split into a set of fragments when it is transferred. The proposed metadata engine is designed so that access to fragment metadata can be minimized when responding to metadata requests from various set-top box applications.

articleTitle: A 9 mW OFDM demodulator LSI for narrow-bandwidth ISDB-T
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We have developed narrow-bandwidth OFDM demodulator LSI for Japanese digital terrestrial broadcasting (ISDB-T) and digital terrestrial sound broadcasting (ISDB-T/sub SB/). We have achieved ultra low power consumption of 9 mW (typical).

articleTitle: System requirements and considerations for visual table of contents in personal video recording
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: With the introduction of non-tape based digital video recorders, consumers can expect alternative navigation methods to the well-known trick-play modes found on analog and digital tape-based systems. In this paper, we explore the system requirements and aspects of the Visual Table of Content (VTOC). One reason for implementing a VTOC search mode is that it provides a much higher visual performance at high search speeds (50 times or higher) than the conventional search techniques. We present a solution based on re-using MPEG-compressed video data to generate the video signal for the visual search. The video search signal is composed of a set of sub-pictures (mosaic screen) each of which is MPEG compressed An efficient strategy is introduced that allows either full or partial re-use of the compressed sub-pictures to allow the generation of a new mosaic screen.

articleTitle: Building MPEG-7 transcoding hints from intrinsic characteristics of MPEG videos
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Transcoding hints are defined in the MPEG-7 standard to provide better quality or reduced complexity of transcoding applications. The paper: 1) defines practical transcoding hint hierarchies from both structural and semantic perspectives; 2) addresses three application scenarios from which transcoding hints can be generated; 3) proposes architectures of transcoding hint generators for different application scenarios, based on retrieved low-level MPEG characteristics.

articleTitle: Development of VCR with ULP (ultra long play) mode
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: In general, the recording time of a VCR with an SP (standard play) head is at most 3 hours on a T-180 tape. This paper describes an advanced VCR technology with an ULP (ultra long play) mode whose recording time is 15 hours on the tape, which is 5 times longer than the SP mode.

articleTitle: Realization of storage-based interactive service "ep" and the receiver integrating digital broadcasting and Internet
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We present storage-based interactive service and the receiver. Contents from digital broadcasting are stored into HDD and updated automatically. This technology enables seamless access between HDD, broadcasting and Internet.

articleTitle: Precombining adaptive-order equalizer for downlink MAI suppression in CDMA systems
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: A new MAI suppression method - precombining adaptive-order equalizer - is proposed for a cellular CDMA system downlink. By means of increasing and smoothing the SNR variation of the input signal and optimizing the equalizer order, it greatly improves the performance of the common equalizer-based MAI suppression receivers in low SNR and fading cases. The proposed approach is especially suitable for 3G high-speed downlink packet access (HSDPA) systems. The receiver structure is described and represented mathematically. The receiver performance is evaluated through simulation and compared with common equalizer-based and RAKE receivers.

articleTitle: An application of autonomous computing for the automotive industry
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: Technologies and services such as Bluetooth/sup TM/, Onstar/sup TM/, Carfax/sup TM/, GPS, black box recorders, electronic keys, and collective distributed computing have all lent their offerings in hopes of contributing to goals of improving the driving experience, whether by combining commuting needs, improving crash survivability, improving trafficking or instant destination rerouting. Each of these technologies requires only the manufacturer, governing laws, and the consumer to implement in order to reap their featured benefits. Autonomous computing is much different in this respect because it will require many more players than any other technology. Additional organizations that must be employed to make this vision a reality are: consumer services organizations, local, and state municipalities, and the National Department of Transportation. This may, if proven effective, be the catalyst in restructuring the automotive insurance industry as a whole.

articleTitle: A user adaptive perceptual rate control scheme for FGS videos
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: MPEG-4 fine-granularity-scalable (FGS) video coding is novel for supporting a continuous bitrate spectrum. We propose a new video quality metric that considers the user's preference of spatial-temporal quality tradeoff. A practical rate control scheme for FGS videos is developed accordingly, to provide constant perceived quality over time.

articleTitle: Design of color-code system for time-stamping broadcast video
publicationTitle: 2003 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics, 2003. ICCE.
abstract: We propose a color-code system to time-stamp TV broadcast video for the purpose of video indexing and monitoring. This scheme can be used for digital broadcast video as well as for analog broadcast video.
